Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

silent adjective

also silently, in silence, say nothing, mute (silent), still (silent), fall silent, become silent, keep something quiet

classical

Plaut. Ep. 5.1.44 (Lewis & Short, s.v. taceō)
Cic. Cat. 1.20: quōrum voluntātem tacitōrum perspicis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 379

tacitus, tacita, tacitum

silent, saying nothing; quiet

Of a person who says nothing, and of things that make no sound; also, passively, unspoken, kept secret (tacitum tenēre, Cic. de Or. 3.64). To be silent is tacēre (see be quiet); silently, tacitē (see silence).

Other words

  • silēns, silentis — still, silent

    also used · classical · Cato Agr. 40.1: lūnā silentī

    Of night, places and the moon; Cato’s lūna silēns is the new moon, when it gives no light.

  • mūtus, mūta, mūtum — mute; silent, still

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.10.2; Cic. post Red. 1.3: mūtum forum, ēlinguem cūriam (Lewis & Short)

    Unable to speak, dumb; of places and times where no sound is heard, silent (see mute).

  • conticēscō, conticēscere, conticuī — fall silent, become silent

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 379

Examples

  • quod bonī est, id tacitus taceās tūte tēcum et gaudeās

    if it’s good news, keep it to yourself, say nothing, and be gladPlaut. Ep. 5.1.44 (Lewis & Short)

  • aut quam sīdera multa, cum tacet nox

    or as many as the stars when the night is silentCatull. 7.7

  • sine tē omnia mea mūta esse

    that without you everything of mine is silentCic. Fam. 16.10.2

  • aliquid tacēre

    to keep something silentTraupman 379

See also silence, be quiet, mute, quiet!.
